analyst.summary: Cholamandalam Investment and Finance had a strong FY26 -- its loan book grew 21% to about Rs 2.43 lakh crore and profit rose almost 23%, with comfortable capital reserves. Growth is increasingly coming from newer, smaller lending lines (property loans, SME, and a newly launched gold-loan business) while its largest business, vehicle finance, is going through a slower patch in commercial-vehicle demand. Its unsecured personal and small-business loan book has seen real stress from over-borrowed customers sourced through digital partners, which management says has peaked and is now improving. A recent regulatory change in how bad loans are counted has also pushed up the headline non-performing-loan number, making the underlying picture somewhat harder to read cleanly against history even though the business itself has not deteriorated by nearly as much as the raw number suggests. At current prices, the stock already reflects a well-run, fast-growing lender, leaving little room for anything to go wrong. We rate it Hold.
